title: Corey Haines' marketing-plan skill: AARRR planning and marketing as a compounding portfolio
summary: Corey Haines' open-source fCMO playbook for building a 12-month marketing plan structured by AARRR and tailored to a company's real budget, team and funding stage. Its spine is marketing as investing: stack compounding assets, diversify, and tie every move to a mechanism and a metric.

principles.text: Treat marketing like investing: build a compounding portfolio of buy-and-hold assets, not a campaign calendar of one-off spikes.
principles.quote: Buy-and-hold assets (SEO content, a newsletter, a community, a referral loop) over one-off spikes. Diversify — no single channel carries the plan. Time in market beats timing the market.

principles.text: No silver bullet exists; win by stacking many small compounding assets.
principles.quote: There is no one move that fixes growth. The plan wins by stacking many small compounding assets.

principles.text: Favor assets with the most downstream reuse: one cornerstone piece should feed search, backlinks, newsletter, social and talks.
principles.quote: A single well-made asset should pay off across the portfolio: a cornerstone piece ranks in search, earns backlinks, feeds the newsletter, seeds social, and becomes a conference talk.

principles.text: Earn attention by being worth it; marketing is non-deterministic, so run a portfolio of bets and double down on what works.
principles.quote: You earn attention by being worth paying attention to — you don't buy your way to a captive audience.

principles.text: Every move needs a named mechanism and leading indicator; if it can't be measured, run it as an experiment with a kill criterion.
principles.quote: Hope is not a strategy. Every move in the plan names its mechanism and its leading indicator.

principles.text: Sanity-check the market first: score the problem on size and frequency; big and frequent problems reward compounding marketing most.
principles.quote: Big-and-frequent problems reward the compounding-portfolio approach most.
